accounting.rationale: PDF128 lines10-11 defines four entity categories for this attribute. Classification is retained without a no-op executable or a duplicate procedure-definition owner.
An attribute declaration identifies a procedure/block-data role; it is not proof of an explicit interface, successful linkage, association status or invocation.
Retain external-procedure identity and the corresponding explicit/implicit interface rules in15.4.3.2/.5/.6. A procedure's being external is distinct from declaring this attribute at a use site.
A dummy procedure is included, with argument correspondence and characteristics governed by15.5.2.10. It is not a dummy data object.
Procedure-pointer declaration and characteristics retain15.4.3.6 ownership. EXTERNAL alone does not establish association or permit a call through an undefined pointer.

Block data is a separate program-unit category, not a callable procedure. Its name in an EXTERNAL statement confirms program membership under15.4.3.5p2; linker conventions are not a new language oracle.
PDF128 lines17-18 gives two procedure categories crossed with two uses. The mandatory declaration is prose; diagnostic obligation is assessed separately under4.2.
Four declaration mechanisms point to normative owners. The note does not require a separate EXTERNAL statement when another mechanism already supplies the attribute.
Attribute specification in8.2 is one mechanism; bare result-type information must not be confused with an EXTERNAL attribute.

15.4.3.2p5 supplies EXTERNAL for an appropriate generic/specific interface body. C844 prohibits specifying it for the same procedure inside that body, not the body's declaration of the attribute in its containing context.
The statement's direct attribute and block-data membership semantics are15.4.3.5p1-p2, not additional independent requirements from this note.
15.4.3.6p1 supplies EXTERNAL for each proc-decl entity. Interface and initialization clauses have separate owners; an explicit interface is not required merely by every procedure declaration.

requirements.title: One entity cannot have both EXTERNAL and INTRINSIC
requirements.definition: EXTERNAL and INTRINSIC cannot both describe the same entity. This does not prohibit two different entities from having the respective attributes, or an appropriately declared external procedure from using the spelling of an intrinsic procedure.

pending.attribute-conflict: PENDING a complete specification context declaring a known eligible specific intrinsic, such as ABS, both INTRINSIC and EXTERNAL. Remove only one attribute declaration for each valid control; do not add a conflicting data declaration, generic-only intrinsic or invalid invocation.
pending.declaration-order: PENDING reversed separate-statement order and the type-declaration EXTERNAL spelling, keeping the same single-entity conflict. Each observed diagnostic must name that conflict at a legitimate statement, rather than any error mentioning an intrinsic.
pending.separate-role-controls: PENDING complete independent intrinsic-only and external-only declarations plus two distinct names with the separate roles. Compatible external definitions are supplied if invoked; compile admission does not prove linkage or intrinsic result semantics.
pending.intrinsic-shadowing-source: PENDING the exact8.5.11/15.3/16.2/19.3 name and specific-intrinsic relations for an explicitly declared external procedure whose spelling matches an intrinsic. Preserve those owners and do not treat spelling alone as the forbidden conjunction.

requirements.oracle: A same-entity attribute conflict with one-attribute repairs and separate-role controls. Bind cause, declared source identity and actual allowed diagnostic locations.
requirements.oracle_limitation: 4.2p2(3) requires reporting capability, not fatal rejection, a particular English sentence or a printed constraint code. Unsupported intrinsic facilities, unrelated name/type recovery, source echoes and native compiler failures cannot satisfy the predicate.

requirements.title: An external subprogram cannot specify EXTERNAL for its own defined procedure
requirements.definition: Within an external subprogram, a procedure defined by that subprogram is not given an EXTERNAL specification there. This is a restriction on the defining scope, not a ban on declaring the procedure EXTERNAL in a caller or on declaring other external procedures in the subprogram.

pending.subroutine-own-name: PENDING a complete external subroutine with an EXTERNAL statement naming itself, repaired only by removing that statement. No recursion, invocation or conflicting dummy/data entity is needed. Preserve actual header/declaration blame sites without coalescing source statements.
pending.function-own-name: PENDING a complete external function with a distinct RESULT name and a defined ordinary INTEGER result, adding only the forbidden EXTERNAL declaration for the function name. Keep function identity distinct from the result variable and avoid an additional result-type defect.
pending.other-procedure-control: PENDING an external subprogram declaring a different external helper and a caller declaring the defined procedure. Any invocation uses compatible characteristics; a different name's legitimate declaration is not a repair that silently removes a required dependency.
pending.entry-scope-source: PENDING exact15.6.2.6/19.3.1/19.3.3 relations for additional procedures defined by ENTRY. Obsolescent reporting remains separate and cannot itself satisfy the own-procedure conflict. Module/internal procedure contexts are not automatically covered by this external-subprogram constraint.

requirements.oracle: Own-procedure declaration negatives with complete one-statement repairs and contrasting external use sites.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Required diagnostic capability does not prescribe fatal status, text or code. A parser rejection of ENTRY, a result-variable error, unrelated scope conflict or recursion limitation is not causal evidence of C843.

requirements.title: An interface body cannot specify EXTERNAL for its own declared procedure
requirements.definition: The procedure declared by an interface body cannot be given an EXTERNAL specification within that body. The interface body can itself supply EXTERNAL in its containing context under15.4.3.2p5; that is a different declaration relationship.

pending.subroutine-interface-own-name: PENDING a complete host with a specific interface body for a subroutine, containing EXTERNAL for that same subroutine name. Remove only the inner declaration. An uninvoked declaration does not require a fake procedure definition or missing-link oracle.
pending.function-interface-own-name: PENDING the corresponding INTEGER function interface using a distinct result name, with only the inner EXTERNAL specification removed by its control. Do not confuse the declared procedure with a result variable or rely on a mismatched external definition.
pending.declaration-source-relations: PENDING finite source relations from8.5.9p1/p2 and15.4.3.2p5 to the containing caller/dummy/procedure-pointer contexts. This resolves the apparent conflict between an interface body supplying the attribute and forbidding its inner respecification, without generating duplicate no-op tests.
pending.other-interface-categories-source: PENDING exact abstract, generic and module-interface body premises from15.4.3.2. Module/abstract identity and independent restrictions must be isolated before a negative is assigned this primary owner.

requirements.oracle: Inner-own-procedure specification negatives, minimal repairs and source-qualified containing-scope attribute relations.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A wrong-scope import, duplicate explicit interface, unsupported separate-module facility or unrelated result declaration is not C844 evidence. Reporting capability has no fatal-exit, exact-English or printed-code requirement.

requirements.title: External and dummy procedure arguments or pointer targets require an EXTERNAL declaration
requirements.definition: An external procedure or dummy procedure used as an actual argument or as the target of procedure pointer assignment must be declared EXTERNAL. A qualifying interface body or procedure declaration can already provide the attribute; a separate EXTERNAL statement is not universally required. The rule does not reclassify internal or module procedures as external.

pending.external-as-actual: PENDING a complete external INTEGER function passed to a compatible explicit-interface recipient, with EXTERNAL supplied at the passing site. If invoked, compare a defined scalar result with an independent literal and retain actual-procedure characteristics; this is a run/positive-control, not a new procedure-call effect owner.
pending.dummy-as-actual: PENDING a complete forwarding procedure whose dummy procedure is declared by EXTERNAL, a qualifying interface body or PROCEDURE, then passed onward. Preserve explicit/implicit interface and type/kind characteristics under15.5.2.10; merely calling a data object is not the intended missing-declaration contrast.
pending.external-as-pointer-target: PENDING a complete compatible procedure-pointer assignment to a declared external target. Establish association before querying/calling the pointer and keep the target lifetime valid. Pointer assignment's characteristics and association effects retain10.2.2.4 ownership.
pending.dummy-as-pointer-target: PENDING the corresponding assignment from a declared nonpointer dummy procedure during a live invocation. Preserve ultimate-argument and host-instance rules; do not escape an internal procedure's host lifetime or fabricate a different effective argument for a nonpointer actual to an IN pointer dummy.
pending.declaration-mechanism-census: PENDING a finite four-mechanism source/use inventory: type declaration with EXTERNAL, generic/specific interface body, EXTERNAL statement and procedure declaration. Map their normative8.2/15.4.3.2/.5/.6 owners and qualifying contexts. Abstract interfaces and bare type declarations are not interchangeable mechanisms.
pending.module-internal-boundaries: PENDING compatible internal/module actuals and procedure targets under their own15.5.2.10/10.2.2.4 conditions. They do not need EXTERNAL merely because the two operations occur. Include block-data classification only as a source relation, not as a callable target.
pending.missing-declaration-reporting-gate: PENDING a case-specific4.2p2 and Clause19 analysis before any missing-attribute diagnosis claim. This prose shall alone does not impose a numbered-constraint diagnostic. Use a separately established numbered/scope owner or explicit compiler policy, not a blanket S-level required rejection or an unrelated implicit-name/type error.

requirements.oracle: Complete declared-procedure positive controls and finite canonical declaration/use relations. Any callback result has independent literal expectations, valid characteristics and live association; the controls demonstrate only their finite admissible contexts.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No compulsory diagnostic is inferred solely from a prose restriction. Existing validators require a separate policy basis for an S-level invalid case without a required standard diagnostic. Source/role gaps stay pending, never bypassed by retagging effects or inventing canonical approval.

review_rationale: Independent original-source and complete pending-plan review14b9e8243c1caefb87948397ed1e28f0d85050e9b22ff67e72dc69514a20cda7, registered in doc/source_audits/batch_053.json. All6base/23fine units and four requirements retain nineteen pending facets. Four EXTERNAL roles include noncallable block data; own-procedure scope restrictions and interface-body attribute provision are distinct. The external/dummy by actual/pointer-target matrix and four declaration mechanisms preserve their canonical owners. Prose declaration restrictions do not become blanket required diagnostics. No fixture, compiler observation or source-use/canonical connection is added or approved.
